workflows.name: Best-of-Breed Product Lifecycle Management, Vendor Release Intake & Exit Reserves

Automation Opportunity: - Intake checklist auto-scores each vendor release against the regression-pack result and the product's upgrade-currency position (replaces manual Step 1–2 collation).
- Exit-reserve accrual auto-computed from license spend at each QBR (replaces manual Step 5 calculation).
Controls: - CTL-569 (ensure controlled execution — Application Portfolio, Integration & Solution Architecture (PA-113.2).)
- operational: vendor releases pass the domain regression pack (Tier-1 mandatory) before production
- operational: upgrade-currency KPI — defer one cycle, never two; Tier & Control Board escalation at two behind
- operational: exit reserve accrued at every QBR; contract clauses (data residency, exit assistance, export, price caps) verified at signature and renewal
Pain Points / Risks: - **Upgrade-debt risk**: deferred vendor releases accumulate until a product is two major versions behind, stacking security and integration exposure; mitigated by the defer-one-never-two rule and the Tier & Control Board escalation at two behind

- **Untested-exit risk**: exit clauses and data-export rights go unexercised until the day they are needed; mitigated by funded exit reserves accrued at every QBR, open-format export clauses, and transition-assistance terms verified at signature and renewal
Staffing Implication: - Absorbed within the sized buy-archetype teams — the 4 Vendor Product Manager seats are already in the OM §9.1 sizing (WLI ×2, SSP ×1, CCP ×1) plus the CIO Office vendor-portfolio analyst; no incremental headcount.
System Touchpoints: - Vendor staging rings & the domain regression pack (Tier-1 coverage mandatory per release)
- Upgrade-currency dashboard (vendor version vs current, per BoB product)
- Exit-reserve ledger (CIO Office central bucket; disclosed in the QBR FinOps pack — links to VS-135)
- TPRM reassessment & continuous-monitoring platform (links to VS-161/W4729/W4734)
- IAP consumer-driven contract tests for product-to-product flows (links to W3579)
Time Estimate: Release intake ~4–8 hours/release × ~6–12 releases/product/year × 9 products ≈ 216–864 hours/year; lifecycle administration (clause reviews, reassessments, reserves, health checks) ~2–4 hours/product/month × 9 products × 12 months ≈ 216–432 hours/year. Total **≈ 432–1,296 hours/year** (≈0.21–0.62 FTE) across the four Vendor PM seats and the CIO Office secretariat.

steps.activity: Vendor Product Manager run release intake: vendor releases land in the owning team's staging ring and pass the intake checklist plus the domain regression pack (Tier-1 workflow coverage mandatory) before production — the same standard the ERP vendor train meets; a release may be deferred one cycle, never two

Vendor PM/IT PO track the upgrade-currency KPI — at most one major version behind vendor current per product; a product two versions behind is a Tier & Control Board escalation with a funded remediation plan

Procurement/Legal/Vendor PM verify the required contract clauses at signature and each renewal: Philippine data-residency/processing terms (RA 10173), statutory-readiness warranty where applicable, exit/transition assistance, data-export in open formats, and price-escalation caps

SEC/TPRM keep every BoB vendor risk-tiered with tier-1 annual reassessment and audit-report review (links to VS-161/W4729); continuous-monitoring feeds (financial, cyber, performance) watch vendor health and EOL (links to W4734)

CIO Office accrue each product's exit reserve at every QBR (a set percentage of license cost, held centrally) and disclose reserves in the QBR FinOps pack — a vendor exit is never unfundable (links to VS-135)

Vendor PM/CIO Office manage product health: SLA attainment, integration latency vs IAP budget, roadmap intelligence, and the Register's re-evaluation triggers (links to W5515); sunset decisions route through W3578 application retirement and the SIB (W5515)

fields.Frequency: Continuous intake; quarterly roadmap re-plan; annual QBR structural review
fields.Participants: Head of EA, owning team IT PO/PM & BPO (the stakeholder's single face), product/process architects, CIO (Product Council chair), FinOps/TBM analyst (links to VS-135), vendor-portfolio analyst, ARB (links to W3571), SEC privacy/TPRM pre-read for customer-data surfaces (links to VS-161), PMO for initiative-sized routing (links to VS-112)
fields.Trigger: A BPO or executive stakeholder raises a new software-capability need with their paired IT PO/PM; a quarterly roadmap re-plan; an annual QBR structural review; or a fired sourcing re-evaluation trigger needing re-triage (links to W5515)
fields.Volume: One front door for the whole 17-product estate — ~40–60 new-capability items/year reach EA triage (routine enhancements resolve in team backlogs at the weekly BPO–PO refinement and never escalate); each quarterly re-plan re-triages 4–8 carried-over items

Automation Opportunity: - Intake triage auto-classifies each logged need against the value-stream catalog and proposes enhancement / gap-admission / sourcing-candidate routing (replaces manual Step 1).
- Intake-register states auto-generate the quarterly Product-Council pack appendix and the stakeholder feedback notes (replaces manual Steps 2 and 6 collation).
Controls: - CTL-569 (ensure controlled execution — Application Portfolio, Integration & Solution Architecture (PA-113.2).)
- operational: every new-capability request carries an accepted/routed/declined state before any procurement or build begins
- operational: sourcing candidates route only through the SIB gate (W5515); no tooling is procured directly from an intake item
Pain Points / Risks: - **Front-door-bypass risk**: a stakeholder bypasses the intake and procures a tool directly, recreating the siloed spend and integration sprawl the sourcing gate prevents; mitigated by the single front door, ITAM/SaaS-estate discovery (links to VS-99) reconciling unregistered products, and the annual QBR reaffirmation exposing them

- **Stalled-demand risk**: raised needs sit without an accepted/routed/declined outcome, pushing stakeholders to escalate around the process; mitigated by the closed-loop state on every logged item and the BPO returning decisions with reasons
Staffing Implication: - Absorbed within the sized CIO Office (Head of EA + vendor-portfolio analyst, OM §5.3/§9.1); the intake formalizes the existing BPO → PO → EA flow ahead of the W5515 gate — no incremental headcount.
System Touchpoints: - Product-backlog intake records across the 17-product estate (single backlogs; the BPO–PO refinement board)
- Capability Sourcing Register feed (accepted sourcing candidates enter the W5515 gate with their triage pack)
- Workflow catalog & value-stream index (coverage-check and gap-admission routing)
- TBM/FinOps cost model (links to VS-135/W4100) — rough-TCO inputs for the triage pack
- SaaS/application discovery (links to VS-99) — shadow-tooling exposure feeding the annual reaffirmation
Time Estimate: Triage and routing ~2–6 hours/item × ~40–60 items/year ≈ 80–360 hours/year; quarterly re-plan/escalation packs ~4 hours/quarter × 4 quarters ≈ 16 hours/year. Total **≈ 96–376 hours/year** (≈0.05–0.18 FTE), absorbed within the CIO Office.

steps.activity: Log the raised need in the owning product's backlog and classify it against the 188-VS catalog: (a) enhancement of an existing product → stays in the team backlog; (b) a missing workflow-level owner inside an existing value stream → owning team + architect for gap-admission; (c) a genuinely new capability or value stream → sourcing-candidate triage (Step 3)
steps.r: Owning PO & BPO / Head of EA

steps.activity: Close the loop with the stakeholder through the BPO: every logged item carries an accepted / routed / declined-with-reason state — a stakeholder never waits on an unacknowledged request

For sourcing candidates, assemble the triage pack: BPO outcome statement & KPIs, the architect's integration sketch over the IAP contract patterns (links to W3579), a rough TCO (links to W4100), compliance constraints (RA 10173 privacy for customer data; BIR official receipts for billed services), and a preliminary Tier proposal

Route the outcome: backlog items → owning-PO prioritization via the roadmap; new-workflow/VS admissions → the workflow-catalog gap-analysis path; new capabilities → a sourcing proposal to the SIB gate (links to W5515); initiative-sized delivery → the PMO (links to VS-112)

Fund and schedule accepted items at the Product Council — capacity is allocated as funding runs, not projects; roadmap approval above PHP 5M; the quarterly re-plan sequences winners into release trains and rings

Keep the intake register state current — accepted/routed/declined outcomes feed portfolio reporting (links to W3592) and the QBR outcome review; declined items return to the stakeholder with the rationale via the BPO
